ab
View examples▶Wagner Mahler R.Strauss
[GM], [RW: Oper], [RS: Oper]
Italian:
da, a partire da — from; from … onward
via, via da — away; off
giù — down (chiefly in military commands)
togliere — remove (in removal instructions)
The choice depends on the sense and context.

Preposition and adverb.

【General meanings】
① From; from ... onward, marking a starting point in time, space, quantity, etc.
② Away; off; leaving. As a stage direction: exit.
③ Detached; off, as of a button.
④ Down; lower, chiefly in military commands.

【Examples in musical contexts】
[GM]
German: Dämpfer allmählich ab
English: Gradually remove the mutes.

[RW: Oper]
German: Sie eilen ab.
English: They hurry off.

[RS: Oper]
German: die ganze Steigerung von hier ab durchaus parodistisch!
English: The whole build-up from here on is to be entirely parodic!

【Usage notes】
“Remove the mute” (Dämpfer ab, Sordinen ab, referring to an external mute; corresponding to senza sordino for string and wind instruments); “From the indicated bar or beat”; “Exit the stage.”

【References】
Duden: ab (adverb) / IDS: ab (preposition)
abdämpfen
View examples▶Mahler
[GM]
Italian:
smorzare, attutire

【General meanings】
① Reduce or soften the strength or effect of sound, vibration, impact, etc.
② Figuratively, subdue or temper the intensity of an emotion or similar response.

【Usage notes】
On percussion instruments, damping reduces or stops the after-ring by restraining the vibration of the head, metal plate or other vibrating part. On timpani, for example, the after-ring can be stopped by touching the head with the hand. The method and timing depend on the instrument, notation and musical context.

【References】
Duden: abdämpfen / VSL: Timpani / Treccani: smorzare
abgestimmte
View examples▶Mahler
[GM]
Italian:
coordinato — coordinated
accordato — tuned
bilanciato — balanced (when referring to balance)
These expressions are similar in meaning; the choice depends on the sense and context.

Abgestimmte is an inflected adjectival form of abgestimmt, the past participle of abstimmen.

【General meanings】
Adjusted, coordinated or brought into agreement with one another or with a given standard; matched or coordinated when referring to clothing, for example.

【Examples in musical contexts】
“Tuned to the required pitches,” referring to bells or other instruments.

In the fifth movement of Mahler's SYMPHONIE III, abgestimmte Glocken refers to bells with the specified pitches.

【References】
IDS: abstimmen / Document held by the International Gustav Mahler Society / Treccani: accordare

Reference score: Mahler, SYMPHONIE III (Universal/Dover edition): printed p. 190 / PDF p. 194
abnehmen
View examples▶Wagner Mahler R.Strauss
[GM], [RS: Oper], [RW: Oper]
Italian:
diminuire, calare — decrease; diminish
togliere, levare — take off; remove

【General meanings】
① Decrease, diminish or wane (in amount, degree, strength, etc.).
② Take off or remove (a hat, glasses, etc.).
③ Decrease in weight; lose body weight.
④ Pick up (the telephone receiver).

【Examples in musical contexts】
[GM]
German: nehmen nach und nach die Dämpfer ab
English: Gradually remove the mutes.

[RW: Oper]
German: Die beiden Fermaten müssen von besonders langer Dauer sein, um nach dem schnelleren Anschwellen ein sehr allmähliches Abnehmen ausführen zu lassen.
English: Both fermatas must be held for a particularly long time, to allow a very gradual diminuendo after the quicker crescendo.

[RS: Oper]
German: Sklavinnen bringen Salben und die sieben Schleier und nehmen Salome die Sandalen ab.
English: The Sklavinnen bring perfumed ointments and the seven veils and remove Salome’s sandals.

【Usage notes】
In the context of a gradual reduction in volume, it corresponds to diminuendo or decrescendo. When used of tempo, it denotes a decrease in speed. Dämpfer abnehmen means “remove the mute(s).”

In GM, the term is used in both senses ① and ②.

【References】
Duden: abnehmen / Mahler Foundation: Terminology
abreißen
View examples▶Mahler R.Strauss
[GM], [RS: Oper]
Italian:
strappare (via) — tear off; rip away
abbattere — demolish
interrompersi — break off; be interrupted (intransitive)
interrompere, troncare — interrupt; cut off (transitive)

【General meanings】
① Transitive: tear off or rip away; demolish (a building).
② Intransitive: break off abruptly, be interrupted, or cease (speech, contact, etc.).

【Examples in musical contexts】
[GM]
German: scharf abreissen
English: Cut off the sound sharply.

[RS: Oper]
German: Er reisst sich das Kranzgewinde ab und wirft es auf den Tisch.
English: He tears the wreath from his head and throws it onto the table.

【Usage notes】
Applied to a note or phrase: “cut off abruptly”; to the musical flow: “break up.” Nicht abreißen means “do not cut off abruptly.”

【References】
Duden: abreißen / Mahler, SYMPHONIE III: Flute 2 part (PDF p. 15 / printed p. 15)
Abstieg
[RS: Alpen]
Descent (from a mountain); a downhill path or slope.

(Verified location in the reference score: RS, Eine Alpensinfonie Op.64: 3 bars before rehearsal 110; page first bar)

abstoßen
[H: KM3]
Italian:
respingere; (mus.) staccare, staccato

【General meanings】
① Push off or away, move something away with a push, or repel (physically).
② Arouse disgust or cause displeasure.
③ Sell off or dispose of (something unwanted).

【Examples in musical contexts】
“Play staccato”; “Detach and separate the notes”; “Play detached notes” (on string instruments).

【Usage notes】
On wind instruments, the notes may be separated by tonguing. The sharpness, length and force of the separation depend on the instrument, articulation marks, tempo, dynamics and surrounding directions.

【References】
Langenscheidt: abstoßen / Dommer's music dictionary: Abstoßen (transcription) / Treccani: staccato

(Reference score: Hindemith, Kammermusik Nr. 3 für obligates Violoncello und 10 Solo-Instrumente Op.36/Nr.2, Schott edition: printed p. 52 / PDF p. 52.)
Abstufungen
View examples▶Mahler
[GM]
Italian:
gradazioni, sfumature, depending on the sense

Abstufungen is the plural of Abstufung.

【General meanings】
① Gradation; differentiation into levels or degrees; differences of degree. When comparing dynamics or tempos, it refers to their gradations or fine distinctions.
② Shades, subtle differences or nuances (of colour, sound, light, etc.); “expressive shadings” when referring to expression.

【References】
Duden: Abstufung / Treccani: sfumatura
abwärts
[B: 3], [B: 5]
Italian:
verso il basso

【General meanings】
“Downwards”; “Downhill”.
abweichen
View examples▶Mahler
[GM]
Italian:
deviare da, scostarsi da — deviate or depart from
differire da — differ from (depending on the sense)

【General meanings】
① Deviate, depart or stray from a course, rule, standard, topic, etc.
② Differ or diverge in form, character, opinion, etc.

The verb commonly takes von with the dative: “depart from” or “differ from.”

【Usage notes】
In music, it can describe differences in dynamics from other parts. When comparing tempos or pitches, it describes a departure from the reference tempo or pitch.

【References】
Duden: abweichen / Langenscheidt: abweichen
accelerando bis --- fest im gewonnenen, lebhaften Zeitmaß

Gradually accelerate, then hold firmly to the lively tempo reached.

(RS, Ein Heldenleben Op.40, bar 176, OGT 230.)

achten
View examples▶Wagner Mahler R.Strauss
[GM], [RW: Oper], [RS: Oper]
Italian:
fare attenzione a, badare a — pay attention to; heed
rispettare, stimare — respect; esteem (according to construction and sense)

【General meanings】
① With auf followed by the accusative: pay attention to, take care with, or heed something.
② With a direct object: respect, esteem, or attach importance to someone or something.

【Examples in musical contexts】
[GM]
German: möglichst zahlreich, aber auf die dynamischen Zeichen sorgfältig achtend
English: With as many players as possible, but observing the dynamic markings carefully.

[RW: Oper]
German: mit der fürchterlichsten Anstrengung, um gehört zu werden, seinen Blick nur auf Lohengrin geheftet und der Andringenden nicht achtend.
English: With the most desperate effort to make himself heard, his gaze fixed solely on Lohengrin, ignoring those pressing in on him.

[RS: Oper]
German: ohne auf Waldner zu achten; nur zu Arabella
English: Ignoring Waldner; only to Arabella.

【Usage notes】
In music, it refers to attention to rhythm, dynamics or instructions. Where the context concerns listening to another part, it can be rendered as “listen carefully to the other parts.”

【References】
IDS: achten auf (pay attention) / IDS: achten (respect rules, rights, etc.) / il Sansoni: achten (German–Italian) / Langenscheidt: achten (German–English)

allgemein
View examples▶Wagner Mahler R.Strauss
[GM], [RW: Oper], [RS: Oper]
Italian:
generale, universale, comune

【General meanings】
① General, overall, universal, or public.
② Generally, on the whole, or widely (when used adverbially).

【Examples in musical contexts】
[GM]
German: Anmerkung für den Dirigenten : Die kleinen Holzbläserfiguren werden ohne Rücksicht auf das allgemeine Ritenuto schneller, nämlich entsprechend dem früheren Tempo ausgeführt. [Anmerkung Mahlers]
English: Note for the conductor: The small woodwind figures (triplets) are played faster, disregarding the general ritenuto, that is, at the earlier tempo (Mahler’s note).

[RW: Oper]
German: Ausbruch allgemeinen Jauchzens.
English: (All the men) burst into cries of joy.

[RS: Oper]
German: Allgemeines, jubelndes Gelächter.

allmählich
View examples▶Wagner Mahler R.Strauss
[GM], [RW: Oper], [RS: Oper]

gradualmente

【General meanings】
Gradually, little by little, or by degrees.

【Examples in musical contexts】
[GM]
German: Allmählich drängend
English: Gradually, with a sense of urgency.

[RW: Oper]
German: Sie wirft die Fackel zur Erde, wo sie allmählich verlischt.
English: She throws the torch to the ground, where it gradually goes out.

[RS: Oper]
German: Der Lärm von vielen Kommenden drinnen, allmählich näher.
English: From inside comes the noise of many approaching people, gradually drawing nearer.

【Usage notes】
In [RW: Oper], the spelling “allmälig” is also found; in [RS: Oper], “allmählig” is also found.

【References】

Almosenier
View examples▶R.Strauss
[RS: Oper]
Italian:
elemosiniere — almoner
cappellano — chaplain (depending on the office)

【General meanings】
① An official responsible for distributing alms and managing the funds or property used for that purpose; historically, an office in a court or church, sometimes held by a cleric.
② Depending on period and region, a title for a chaplain serving a court, the armed forces or an institution.

【Usage notes】
In Der Rosenkavalier Op.59, he is a priest accompanying Baron Ochs; the libretto describes him as an assistant priest from a village.

For the servants in Der Rosenkavalier Op.59, see the entry “Haushofmeister”.

【References】

als
View examples▶Wagner Mahler R.Strauss
[GM], [RW: Oper], [RS: Oper]
Italian:
di, che — than (with a comparative)
come, da — as; in the capacity of
quando — when
come se — as if
The choice depends on the sense and context.

【General meanings】
① Than, with a comparative.
② As; in the capacity or role of.
③ When, referring to a single past event or a state lasting for a period in the past.
④ As if, in constructions such as als ob and als wenn.

【Examples in musical contexts】
[GM]
German: Die 𝅘𝅥 plötzlich etwas langsamer als vorher
English: The quarter notes are suddenly a little slower than before.

[RW: Oper]
German: Elsa ist, als die Züge das Gemach verlassen haben, wie überselig Lohengrin an die Brust gesunken. Lohengrin setzt sich, während der Gesang verhallt, auf einem Ruhebett am Erkerfenster nieder, indem er Elsa sanft nach sich zieht.
English: When the processions have left the bedchamber, Elsa has sunk against Lohengrin’s breast as if in rapture. While the singing dies away, Lohengrin sits down on a couch by the bay window, gently drawing Elsa towards him as he does so.

[RS: Oper]
German: den Dolch in der Faust, kommt von außen hereingestürzt als ein Verfolgender
English: Dagger clenched in his fist, rushes in from outside like a pursuer.

【References】
Duden: als / IDS: temporal als / PONS: German–Italian als
also
View examples▶Mahler R.Strauss
[GM], [RS: Oper]
Italian:
dunque, quindi — therefore; consequently
cioè — that is; namely
allora — well; now then
così — thus; in this way (archaic use)
The choice depends on the sense and context.

【General meanings】
① Therefore; consequently; so.
② That is; namely; in other words.
③ Well; now then, introducing a topic or taking up an earlier one.
④ Archaically, thus; in this way.

【Usage notes】
In RS's title Also sprach Zarathustra Op.30, also has meaning ④: “Thus Spoke Zarathustra.”

【References】

[RS: Oper], [RS: Zara]
Italian:
devozione — devotion; piety
raccoglimento — inner concentration
preghiera, breve funzione religiosa — prayer; a short religious service
These expressions are similar in meaning; the choice depends on the sense and context.

【General meanings】
① Devotions; prayers; a short service centred on prayer.
② Devotion; piety; concentration of the mind in prayer.
③ Inner concentration; absorbed, attentive involvement.

【Examples in musical contexts】
[RS: Oper]
German: mit Andacht
English: Devoutly.

【Usage notes】
Mit Andacht: “devoutly”; “prayerfully”; “with reverence”; also “with deep concentration.”

Anfang
View examples▶Wagner Mahler R.Strauss
[GM], [RW: Oper], [RS: Oper]
Italian:
inizio, principio

【General meanings】
① Beginning; start; opening; early stage.
② Origin; inception.

【Examples in musical contexts】
[GM]
German: Wie von Anfang
English: As at the beginning.

[RW: Oper]
German: Gurnemanz am Anfang der Tafel links.
English: Gurnemanz stands at the head of the table on the left.

[RS: Oper]
German: wieder ruhig, wie zu Anfang
English: Calm again, as at the beginning.

【Usage notes】
Wie im Anfang means “as at the beginning”; when it calls for a return to the opening tempo, it corresponds to Tempo I (tempo primo).
Vom Anfang means “from the beginning”; when directing a repeat from the start of the piece, it corresponds to da capo.

【References】

indicato, stabilito

【General meanings】
Declared; specified; stated; indicated.

【Examples in musical contexts】
[GM]

View examples▶Wagner Mahler
[GM], [RW: Oper], [RS: Oper]
Italian:
fermato — stopped
trattenuto, ritenuto — held back (when referring to tempo)
sostenuto — sustained (when referring to a sustained note)

① Stopped; brought to a halt.
② Urged or instructed to do something.

[RW: Oper]

【Usage notes】

View examples▶Wagner R.Strauss

anhalten
View examples▶Wagner Mahler
[GM], [RW: Oper], [RS: Oper]
Italian:
fermare, arrestare, trattenere

【General meanings】
① To stop (a person or vehicle); to bring to a halt; to call someone to a stop.
② To hold (one's breath).
③ To continue; to persist (of a state, the weather, etc.).
④ To train or urge (someone to do something).

【Examples in musical contexts】
[GM]
German: Anmerkung für den Dirigenten und Sänger : bedeutet hier nur ein kurzes Anhalten auf dem Taktstrich und nicht etwa eine Fermate. [Anmerkung Mahlers]
English: Note for the conductor and singer: Here the symbol indicates only a brief pause at the barline, not a fermata (Mahler’s note).

[RW: Oper]
German: Etwas anhalten.
English: With a slight pause.

[RS: Oper]
German: hält an, ganz in sein Bild versunken
English: He pauses in his singing, completely absorbed in the scene he has evoked.

【Usage notes】
“To hold back (the tempo)”; “to restrain (ritenuto)”; “to pause”; “to sustain (a note).”

In GM, anhalten is rendered as “slower”; in RW, as “with a pause,” among other translations. It can describe holding back or momentarily stopping something already in motion. In musical contexts, its nuance can be close to the Italian ritenuto (slower; restrained), firmly holding the tempo back at that moment.

Footnote example
The noun Anhalten is rendered here as “a pause.” A footnote to Mahler's Das himmlische Leben, a setting of a poem from Des Knaben Wunderhorn, reads “𝄐 bedeutet hier nur ein kurzes Anhalten auf dem Taktstrich und nicht etwa eine Fermate.” In the GM entry, this passage is translated as “Here the symbol 𝄐 indicates only a brief pause at the barline, not a fermata”.

Performance interpretation
This brief pause can also be understood as applying the brakes to the forward motion of the music and momentarily holding it back. One possible performance interpretation is restraint accompanied by an inner tension, like deliberately holding one's breath (Atem anhalten).

Gehalten can refer to sustaining tone and phrasing, in a sense close to tenuto or sostenuto, as well as to restraining the tempo or expression. Its distinction from anhalten depends on the particular use and the surrounding context. See also the entry for gehalten.

anreißen
View examples▶Mahler
[GM]
Italian:
strappare; pizzicare
The choice depends on the sense and context.

【General meanings】
① Make a small tear in the edge of cloth or paper; open a package and begin using its contents.
② Introduce or briefly touch on a topic.
③ Scribe or mark lines on a workpiece, especially metal.
④ Strike and light a match (regional usage).

【Examples in musical contexts】
“Pluck (a string).”

【Usage notes】
In bar 401 of the third movement of Mahler’s SYMPHONIE VII, so stark anreißen asks the cellos and double basses to pluck strongly enough for the strings to strike the fingerboard.

anschlagen
View examples▶Mahler
[GM], [RS: Oper]
Italian:
battere, suonare — strike; sound; play
toccare i tasti — play the keys
urtare contro — hit; come into contact with
The choice depends on the sense and context.

【General meanings】
① Sound a bell, key or stringed instrument by striking, playing or plucking it; sound a note or play a melody.
② Post or put up a handbill or poster.
③ Estimate or assess a price or value.
④ Take effect or work, of a medicine or treatment; bark in warning, of a dog.
⑤ Hit or come into contact with something.
⑥ Adopt or change a pace, tempo or manner of speaking.

【Usage notes】
At bar 401 of the third movement of Mahler’s SYMPHONIE VII, the cellos and double basses are instructed: So stark anreißen, daß die Saiten an das Holz anschlagen. This means to pluck strongly enough for the strings to strike the wood (the fingerboard). Anreißen describes the plucking action; anschlagen describes the strings striking the fingerboard.

【References】
Duden: anschlagen / PONS: anschlagen (German–Italian) / Cambridge: anschlagen / Mahler SYMPHONIE VII: Ünlü, Figure 56, p.100

auf und ab
View examples▶Wagner Mahler R.Strauss
[GM], [RW: Oper], [RS: Oper]
Italian:
su e giù — up and down
avanti e indietro — back and forth
The choice depends on the sense and context.
A combination of auf and ab.

【General meanings】
① Up and down; back and forth.
② As the noun das Auf und Ab: rises and falls, ups and downs, or fluctuations.

【Examples in musical contexts】
[GM]
German: Pater ecstaticus (auf und abschwebend)
English: Ecstatic Father (floating up and down).

[RW: Oper]
German: Er hält sich die Ohren zu und geht verzweiflungsvoll, sich mit sich beratend, die Gasse vor dem Fenster auf und ab.
English: He covers his ears and, in despair, walks up and down the lane in front of the window, deliberating with himself.

[RS: Oper]
German: gleichfalls auf und ab rennend
English: Likewise running up and down.

【Usage notes】
In bar 164 of the Andante of Mahler’s SYMPHONIE VI (listed as movement III in this resource), auf- und abwogend means “moving in rising and falling waves.” Wogen means to surge or move up and down in waves.
In Part II of SYMPHONIE VIII, at bar 219, Pater ecstaticus (auf und abschwebend) describes the character floating up and down. Schweben means to float, drift or remain suspended in the air.
In [RW: Oper] and [RS: Oper], the phrase is rendered as “back and forth” or “up and down,” according to the movement being described.

【References】
Duden: auf_Adverb_vorwaerts_offen / Larousse: auf und ab / Duden: wogen / Duden: schweben / Jürgen Meyer: Reflections on the spatial sound imagination of composers / Mahler: SYMPHONIE VIII, score p.90 (PDF p. 88 / printed p. 90)

German: Roter Schein flammt auf, Fackeln von allen Seiten. Apollo nimmt seine Waffen wieder auf; die Schale küßt er, dann wirft er sie abseits. Aus dem Dickicht von überall die Schäfer mit Fackeln. An ihrer Spitze Peneios, unter ihnen Maskierte. Von der Seite des Hauses gleichzeitig ein Aufzug der Frauen mit Amphoren und Schüsseln, auf dem Kopfe getragen. Voran Gäa mit einem Fruchtkorbe. Die beiden Züge begegnen einander auf der Bühne.
English: A red glow flares up, with torches on all sides. Apollo takes up his weapons again, kisses the bowl and throws it aside. Shepherds with torches emerge from the thickets on all sides, led by Peneios, with masked figures among them. At the same time a procession of women comes from the house, carrying amphorae and bowls on their heads, led by Gäa with a basket of fruit. The two processions meet onstage.

AV
An abbreviation for the thematic catalogue of Richard Strauss's works compiled by Erich Hermann Müller von Asow (Asow-Verzeichnis), and for the catalogue numbers used in it.

The differences between TrV and AV, and why two catalogues exist: their purposes and roles

Some works by Richard Strauss (1864–1949) have opus numbers assigned during his lifetime, but many of his early and late works, studies, occasional pieces, songs, and other compositions have no opus number. Later scholars therefore compiled catalogues to organize and identify his complete output systematically. The principal examples are AV (Asow numbers) and TrV (Trenner numbers). The background to their coexistence, and their respective characteristics and roles, are as follows.

1. AV (Asow-Verzeichnis / Müller von Asow numbers)
Compiler: Erich Hermann Müller von Asow
Full title: Richard Strauss: Thematisches Verzeichnis (three volumes, issued in instalments between 1955 and 1974)
Characteristics and role: A substantial thematic catalogue (a catalogue giving the opening notes of musical themes), published after Richard Strauss's death, and a large-scale catalogue of his works.
It serves as a scholarly reference work and collection of source information, covering in great detail the thematic incipits of individual works, instrumentation, circumstances of composition, locations of autograph manuscripts, dates and performers of first performances, early printed editions, and other information. Müller von Asow died while compiling the third volume, which was supplemented and completed by Alfons Ott and Franz Trenner. The works are divided into categories, including those with and without opus numbers, and arranged chronologically within those categories. Besides works without opus numbers, the third volume includes lost works, arrangements, fragments, unrealized projects, and other material.

2. TrV (Trenner-Verzeichnis / Trenner numbers)
Compiler: Franz Trenner
Full title: Richard Strauss: Werkverzeichnis (published in 1985 / a 1993 version including thematic incipits, and a second revised edition in 1999, completed and continued by Florian Trenner)
Characteristics and role: Incorporating research and information about the works that followed the publication of Müller von Asow's catalogue, this catalogue reorganized the works as a whole in order of composition (chronological order). Its chronological arrangement (from the earliest studies of 1870 to the final works of 1949) is useful for tracing the development of Richard Strauss's creative activity and establishing and identifying dates of composition. The Richard-Strauss-Quellenverzeichnis (Richard Strauss Sources Catalogue / RSQV) takes TrV as its starting point and corrects and supplements the information about the works. TrV is also referenced in research and scholarly editions such as Richard Strauss Werke. Kritische Ausgabe (the critical edition of Richard Strauss's works), although information based on either catalogue may require correction in the light of subsequent research.

In summary:
AV: A comprehensive thematic catalogue (Thematisches Verzeichnis) for investigating thematic incipits, detailed historical and bibliographical information, and the circumstances in which works were composed.
TrV: A chronological catalogue of works (Chronologisches Werkverzeichnis) that orders and identifies the works as a whole chronologically on the basis of research available at the time of publication.

Thus, the catalogues differ in their origins and organization: an earlier, detailed thematic catalogue (AV), followed by a catalogue (TrV) that reorganized the works as a whole chronologically in light of subsequent research. However, AV also uses chronological ordering within its categories, and versions of TrV from 1993 onward also contain thematic incipits. They are consulted as complementary resources, and there are examples of both numbers appearing together in the official list of works.

【References】
- RSQV editorial guidelines (pp. 1 and 6)
- IFB review: Richard-Strauss-Werkverzeichnis

【Usage notes】
“Accompanying”; “following the solo part”; “supporting the main melody”.

“Begleitende Stimmen” means “accompanying parts”.

【General meanings】

[GM]
German: womöglich mehrfach besetzt
English: With several players, if possible.

[RW: Oper]
German: Sobald sich Musiker genug vorfinden, um die 3 Piccoli mehrfach zu besetzen, so sind sie auf der Bühne und zwar in der Nähe des holländischen Schiffes zu placiren; kann man sie jedoch nur einfach besetzen, so sind sie in das Orchester zu stellen.
English: If there are enough musicians to assign more than one player to each of the three piccolo parts, the players are to be placed on stage near Holländer’s ship. If only one player can be assigned to each part, they are to be placed in the orchestra pit.

[RS: Oper]
German: Ich stelle es dem Ermessen des Dirigenten frei, die 4 Lakaien, wenn dieselben nicht durch tüchtige Solisten zu besetzen sind, zu verdoppeln, sogar zu verdreifachen, wobei es sich vielleicht empfiehlt, dem ersten Tenor ein oder zwei Altstimmen beizugeben.
English: If the four footmen’s roles cannot be cast with capable soloists, I leave it to the conductor’s discretion to have each role sung by two or even three singers. In that case it may be advisable to add one or two alto singers to the first tenor.

The gerundio (a non-finite verb form that can be used adverbially) of Italian bisbigliare, meaning to whisper, speak softly, or whisper in someone's ear. As a direction, it means “in a whispering manner” and can also suggest a soft rustling or murmuring sound, like leaves or water.
【Musical meaning】
On the harp, a soft, delicate tremolo produced by lightly and rapidly plucking the strings in repetition.

【Usage notes】
It is usually played with both hands, alternating rapidly between the notes of a chord, for example. To repeat a single pitch, two strings tuned enharmonically to the same pitch can be used.
In the Boosey & Hawkes full score of [RS: Duett] (plate 16629, p. 17), the harp is marked “bispiglando” at the beginning of the Andante. The corresponding passage in the publisher's harp part (plate 16541, p. 1) reads “bisbigliando”.

breit
View examples▶Wagner Mahler R.Strauss
[GM], [RW: Oper], [RS: Oper], [RS: Hr2], [H]
Italian:
largo, largamente, ampio

【General meanings】
① Broad, wide, extensive (in width, area, etc.).
② Lengthy, detailed, long-winded (of speech, descriptions, etc.).
③ (Of a laugh or similar expression, depending on context) brazen, coarse, or unpleasant.

【Examples in musical contexts】
[GM]
German: immer breiter!
English: Ever more unhurriedly!

[RW: Oper]
German: Niemals eilen! Eher breiter werden!
English: Never hurry! Rather, become broader!

[RS: Oper]
German: sich breit vor die Tür stellend
English: Planting himself squarely in front of the door.

【Usage notes】
Depending on context: “broadly”, “unhurriedly (in a largo-like sense)”, “majestically”, “slowly (in tempo)”, “weightily”, “fully sustaining (the notes)”.

It is often translated into Japanese as “broadly”, but as that can seem rather unclear, I use “unhurriedly”. Its nuance may be close to allargando. However, allargando describes a gradual slowing of the tempo, whereas breit does not necessarily call for such a change. When applied to string playing, “breit gestrichen” means something like “with broad bow strokes”. For breit alone, “with a sense of breadth” may also be suitable. “nicht breit” may also suggest keeping the tempo taut. It may, however, ask a particular part not to broaden its notes or rhythm too much, rather than require a change in the overall tempo.

Italian:

Present participle of dahinhuschen.

【General meanings】
① (Of a small animal, shadow, etc.) To dart or whisk past quickly, often silently.

【Examples in musical contexts】

The examples involving wind or an apparition are metaphors for swift, fleeting motion. The word does not necessarily prescribe a particular dynamic level or the fastest possible tempo. Dämpfer
View examples▶Wagner Mahler R.Strauss
[GM], [RS: Oper], [RW: Oper]
Italian:
sordina — mute (for a string or wind instrument)
smorzatore — piano damper
The choice depends on the sense and context.

【General meanings】
① A device that reduces vibration, sound, or impact; a buffer or shock absorber.
② A damper on enthusiasm; a letdown; something that takes the wind out of one's sails.
③ Regionally, a steamer for cooking.
【Musical meanings】
① A mute for a string or wind instrument (sordina), reducing volume and changing the tone colour.
② A piano damper (smorzatore), which stops a string's vibration by coming into contact with it.

【Usage notes】
For removable mutes, mit Dämpfer means “with the mute on” (con sordino), and Dämpfer ab / weg means “remove the mute” (senza sordino). See also “Dämpfer auf.”

【References】
Duden: Dämpfer / Langenscheidt: German–English Dämpfer / Treccani: smorzatore
Dämpfer ab
View examples▶Mahler
[GM]
Short for “Dämpfer abnehmen” or “Dämpfer absetzen.” See “Dämpfer auf.”
Dämpfer auf
View examples▶Mahler
[GM]
Put the mute on

In GM, Dämpfer auf is an instruction equivalent to Dämpfer aufsetzen (to put the mute on). By contrast, Dämpfer ab corresponds to Dämpfer abnehmen or Dämpfer absetzen and means 「remove the mute」.

Here, auf denotes the action of attaching the mute to the instrument. For example, on string instruments the mute is attached to the bridge, while on brass instruments it is fitted to the bell. Dämpfer auf／Dämpfer ab thus form a pair of instructions meaning 「put the mute on／take the mute off」.

On the other hand, auf can also generally mean 「open」. When offen (open) or gestopft (stopped) is indicated for brass instruments, its relationship to open tones, hand-stopping, the use of a mute, and so forth must be interpreted according to the instrument and the surrounding context. The auf in Dämpfer auf does not denote this sense of 「open」, but rather the fitting of the mute.

【References】
Dunstan: Dämpfer (p.105)／Treccani: sordina／Vienna Symphonic Library: Horn

dasselbe
View examples▶Wagner Mahler R.Strauss
[GM], [RW: Oper], [RS: Oper]
Italian:
lo stesso, il medesimo

【General meanings】
The same thing; the identical thing; remaining unchanged.

【Usage notes】
Dasselbe Zeitmaß / Tempo means “the same tempo” (l'istesso tempo).

Derselbe and dieselbe are forms with the same meaning, varying according to gender, number, and case. Dasselbe is the neuter singular nominative or accusative form and may be used either with a noun or on its own.
There is also a use different from the above. In somewhat older or more formal prose, such as that found in [RW: Oper] and [RS: Oper], dasselbe (“that very thing,” “the aforementioned thing”) may be used instead of es (“it”), to refer back to the object and avoid repeating the noun. This use does not necessarily emphasize the referent.

demütig
View examples▶Wagner R.Strauss
[RW: Oper], [RS: Oper]
Italian:
umile, sottomesso

【General meanings】
① Humble, modest, reverent, or self-abasing (toward God or another person).
② Submissive, accepting, or unassuming.

【Examples in musical contexts】
[RW: Oper]
German: Er nähert sich, sehr demütig, langsam Sachs.
English: He slowly approaches Sachs, very humbly.

[RS: Oper]
German: Freihild, die des Narren Botschaft vollständig teilnamlos entgegengenommen hat bei den letzten Worten Guntrams grosse innere Bewegung verraten, jetzt blickt sie zum ersten Male mit wehmütigem Lächeln, das allmählich dem Ausdruck demütiger Ergebenheit weicht, zu Guntram auf.
English: Freihild, who had received the message from der Narr with complete indifference, has revealed great inner agitation at Guntram’s last words. Now, for the first time, she looks up at Guntram with a wistful smile, which gradually gives way to an expression of humble resignation.

【Usage notes】
“humbly,” “with humility,” “reverently,” “meekly,” “bowing the head humbly (where a bowing gesture is specified in the context).”

demütig: humble or reverent (neutral to somewhat positive).
devot: excessively submissive / servile / obsequious (with a strongly negative connotation).
In modern German, devot appears to carry a strong suggestion of servility and ingratiating submission to another person.

This comparison describes a relative tendency in connotation: demütig can also express submissiveness or self-abasement, while devot has an older sense meaning “humble”. Bowing the head is not an inherent requirement of demütig itself.

[RS: Oper]
Italian:
sottomesso, servile, umile

【General meanings】
① (Of a manner) excessively humble, servile, submissive, subservient.
② (Archaic) devout, devoted.

【Examples in musical contexts】
[RS: Oper]
German: sehr devot
English: Very deferentially.

【Usage notes】
“Obsequiously,” “humbly,” “as if rubbing one’s hands in ingratiation,” “submissively,” “(excessively) deferentially,” “bowing and scraping.”

It is rendered as “humbly,” among other possibilities.
Demütig: humble, reverent (neutral to mildly positive).
Devot: excessively submissive / servile / ingratiating (strongly negative in connotation).
In modern German, devot seems to have a strong sense of being servile and eager to please the other person.

This comparison describes a relative tendency in connotation: demütig can also express submissiveness or self-abasement. Sense ② of devot represents historical usage and should be distinguished from its modern general meaning. The examples “as if rubbing one’s hands in ingratiation” and “bowing and scraping” figuratively convey an excessively deferential manner; devot itself does not necessarily prescribe hand-rubbing or bowing.

“With a muffled tone”; “muffled (in sound)”; “dully”; “with a dulled resonance”; “with a muffled sound (on timpani, etc.)”; “gloomily (cupo)”; “with a dark tone”.

Applied to an instrument or voice, the word describes a muffled, dull sound; applied to a character’s feelings or the atmosphere of a scene, it conveys gloom or oppressiveness. ② Sparse; weak or thin (of a voice); dilute or watery (of a liquid).

【Examples】
In Hindemith’s Symphonie in Es für großes Orchester, Sehr dünnen Stahlstab (Stricknadel) means “a very thin steel rod (a knitting needle).” Dünnen is the masculine accusative singular form modifying Stahlstab and describes the thinness of the rod.

【Usage notes】
Historical dictionaries also record a verb dünnen meaning “to thin out or weaken.”

[GM], [RW: Oper], [RS: Oper]

【General meanings】
① Entirely; completely; thoroughly; absolutely. Emphasizes degree or thoroughness: all the way; emphatically.
② At all costs; under all circumstances; by all means; without fail.
③ (Emphasizing an affirmative statement) Certainly; indeed; quite.
④ (With a negative) By no means; not at all.

【Examples in musical contexts】
“Throughout”; “consistently throughout”; “all the way through”.

【Usage notes】
In musical directions, durchaus and durchweg (also durchwegs) can overlap in the sense of “throughout” or “consistently”.
● durchaus:
Emphasizes degree or thoroughness, as in “absolutely” or “without fail”. It can reinforce determination, a state or a quality, and can also be rendered “throughout” in music.
● durchweg (or durchwegs):
Emphasizes consistency over time or space: “throughout” or “without exception”, with the same state maintained across the whole.

【General meanings】
① Simple, plain, uncomplicated, unelaborate.
② Modest, unadorned, unpretentious.
③ Easy, straightforward, readily understood.
④ (Adverbially or for emphasis) Simply, merely, just, absolutely.
⑤ Single, single-fold; not double or multiple.

【Examples in musical contexts】
[GM]
German: Sehr einfach und schlicht wie eine Volksweise
English: Very plainly and simply, like a folk tune.

[RW: Oper]
German: Sobald sich Musiker genug vorfinden, um die 3 Piccoli mehrfach zu besetzen, so sind sie auf der Bühne und zwar in der Nähe des holländischen Schiffes zu placiren; kann man sie jedoch nur einfach besetzen, so sind sie in das Orchester zu stellen.
English: If there are enough musicians to assign more than one player to each of the three piccolo parts, the players are to be placed on stage near Holländer’s ship. If only one player can be assigned to each part, they are to be placed in the orchestra pit.

[RS: Oper]
German: Kommandant wendet sich an der Treppe noch einmal und ruft in einfachem Kommandoton: Befehl!
English: The commandant turns once more at the stairs and calls in a straightforward commanding tone: “Orders!”

【Usage notes】
“Simply (semplice)”; “with simplicity”; “without ornamentation”; “plainly (without elaborate display)”; “without excessive emotion (when accompanied by directions to avoid sentimentality or exaggeration).”

As an expressive direction, it indicates simplicity or an unadorned manner. In the GM entries, it means “simple” or “plain.” When accompanied by ohne Sentimentalität or ohne Pathos, it also calls for the avoidance of sentimentality or exaggerated emotion.

In directions concerning the allocation of parts or players, it may mean “single” or “one player to each part.” At bar 458 of Don Juan Op.20, einfach in the second violins and violas directs the players to end the three-part divisi and return to unison within each section. The wording and musical context determine whether expression or the allocation of parts is intended.

【Usage notes】
“Keep the prescribed tempo or rhythm”; “observe the instruction”; “pause in playing or in an action”; “hold back or slacken the tempo.”

In the GM entries, the present participle einhaltend directs the performers to hold back and ease the music’s forward movement, and is translated as “slacken the tempo.” In stage directions, it can also mean to stop playing or pause in an action. The wording and surrounding context show what is to be maintained, what action is to stop, or what movement is to be checked.

English: “＋” is the sign for individual stopped notes.

[RW: Oper]
German: Die Gesandten Mailands, der lombardischen Städte, Neapels, Ungarns, Böhmens und Baierns treten einzeln, ein jeder mit glänzendem Gefolge von Herolden, auf, werden durch Baroncelli Rienzi vorgestellt u. überreichen ein Schreiben.

【Usage notes】
“Individual notes or trills”; “one player or singer at a time”; “selected players or singers from an ensemble or chorus”; “solo (where each part is assigned to one performer).”

Thus, 4 einzelne Violinen means “four solo violins,” while einzelne gestopfte Töne refers to “individual stopped notes.” In choral directions, Einzelne may refer to selected members of the chorus.

English: Do not be a fool. We shall not be the only ones; even people quite different from the two of us will be wearing disguises.

[RS: Oper]
German: Sonnige Helle dringt ein, es ist alles ein einziges wogendes Menschenmeer
English: Bright sunlight floods in; all is one vast, surging sea of people.

【Usage notes】
Die einzige ... means “the only ...”.
einzuhalten
[B: 8-1]
Italian:
osservare, mantenere — observe; maintain
da osservare, da mantenere — to be observed; to be maintained
The zu-infinitive of einhalten. In an instruction such as ist/sind ... einzuhalten, it means that something is to be observed or maintained.

【General meanings】
① To observe or keep rules, promises, etc.; to maintain a prescribed speed, etc.
② To stop an action, interrupt it, or pause.

【Examples in musical contexts】
“Observe the prescribed tempo, playing technique, etc.”; “observe precisely (in genau einzuhalten)”; “observe strictly (in streng einzuhalten).”

【Usage notes】
In [B: 8-1] (Bruckner’s VIII. Symphonie c-Moll, 1887 version), it is used in sense ①. At rehearsal mark Bb in the finale, NB Bei den Streichern sind die Stricharten genau einzuhalten means “Note: the strings must observe the bowing instructions precisely.”

【References】
Duden: einhalten
IDS grammis: sein / haben with a zu-infinitive
Bruckner, VIII. Symphonie c-Moll, 1887 version, printed p. 190 (PDF p. 194)

Italian:

Past participle of entstellen.

【General meanings】

② Distorted, misrepresented, or garbled (of facts, meaning, content, etc.).

English: Night has fully fallen. Tannhäuser enters, wearing torn pilgrim's clothing, his face pale and haggard; he walks with weary steps, leaning on his staff.

【Usage notes】
“Distorted in sound or expression”; “with a strangely altered sound”; “with a distorted expression.”

In [RS: Till], it appears as an expressive direction attached to a clarinet phrase. In stage directions, it can also describe a person’s appearance: in Tannhäuser in [RW: Oper], sein Antlitz ist bleich und entstellt is translated as “his face is pale and haggard.”

Erleichterung
[RS: Dom]
Italian:
sollievo, alleggerimento, facilitazione

【General meanings】
① Relief or alleviation of pain, burdens, worries, etc.
② Relief, reassurance, or a feeling of release.
③ Making something easier; a means of reducing difficulty or effort; simplification.

【Examples in musical contexts】
“Relief of tension or effort”; “with relief (in mit Erleichterung, etc.)”; “reduction of technical difficulty”; “an easier alternative.”

【Usage notes】
In [RS: Dom], Erleichterung labels a notated alternative intended to make the passage easier to perform. Four bars before rehearsal figure 151, the trombone phrase is redistributed between the first and second players. erschöpft
View examples▶Wagner R.Strauss
[RW: Oper], [RS: Oper]
Italian:
esaurito, sfinito
Past participle of erschöpfen.

【General meanings】
① Exhausted; completely worn out.
② (Of resources, etc.) used up; depleted.

【Examples in musical contexts】
[RW: Oper]
German: Senta setzt sich erschöpft in den Lehnstuhl nieder; bei dem Beginn von Erik's Erzählung versinkt sie wie in magnetischen Schlaf, so dass es scheint als träume sie den von ihm erzählten Traum ebenfalls. - Erik steht an den Stuhl gelehnt zur Seite.
English: Exhausted, Senta sits down in the armchair. As Erik begins his story, she seems to sink into a magnetic sleep (i.e. a state resembling hypnosis, evoking the mesmerism popular in the nineteenth century), so that it appears she too is dreaming the dream he is recounting. Erik stands beside the chair, leaning against it.

[RS: Oper]
German: erschöpft auf einen Stuhl sinkend
English: Sinking exhausted onto a chair.

【References】
Duden: erschöpfen
Langenscheidt: erschöpft
erschreckt
View examples▶Wagner R.Strauss
[RW: Oper], [RS: Oper]
Italian:
spaventato, impaurito
Past participle of erschrecken.

【General meanings】
Startled or frightened (by someone or something).

【Examples in musical contexts】
[RW: Oper]
German: erschreckt auffahrend
English: Starting up in alarm.

[RS: Oper]
German: erschreckt
English: In fear.

【Usage notes】
“Erschreckt” is chiefly the past participle of the transitive verb meaning “to frighten someone,” whereas “erschrocken” is chiefly the past participle of the intransitive verb meaning “to become frightened.” The distinction is between “having frightened / having been frightened” and “having taken fright.” In adjectival descriptions of a state, however, their meanings overlap and cannot be separated absolutely.

【References】
Duden: Flexion von erschrecken
IDS: erschrecken I
erschrocken
View examples▶Wagner R.Strauss
[RW: Oper], [RS: Oper]
Italian:
spaventato, atterrito
Past participle of erschrecken.

【General meanings】
Startled; surprised; frightened.

【Examples in musical contexts】
[RW: Oper]
German: Brangäne erhebt sich erschrocken und verwirrt. Isolde sucht mit furchtbarer Anstrengung sich zu fassen.
English: Brangäne rises, startled and confused. Isolde tries with tremendous effort to regain her composure.

[RS: Oper]
German: Diemut hat sich erschrocken losgerungen und flüchtet, von den 3 Gespielinnen lachend umringt, auf die Stufen vor ihrem Hause.
English: Having broken free in alarm, Diemut flees to the steps in front of her house, surrounded by the laughing 3 Gespielinnen.

【Usage notes】
“Erschreckt” is chiefly the past participle of the transitive verb meaning “to frighten someone,” whereas “erschrocken” is chiefly the past participle of the intransitive verb meaning “to become frightened.” The distinction is between “having frightened / having been frightened” and “having taken fright.” In adjectival descriptions of a state, however, their meanings overlap and cannot be separated absolutely.

erschüttert
View examples▶Wagner R.Strauss
[RW: Oper], [RS: Oper]
Italian:
scosso, commosso, sconvolto
Past participle of erschüttern.

【General meanings】
① (Of buildings, etc.) shaken; rocked; destabilized.
② (Emotionally) deeply shocked; intensely shaken; profoundly moved.

【Examples in musical contexts】
[RW: Oper]
German: Er steht auf, und schreitet auf den Herd zu. Sieglinde blickt erbleichend und tief erschüttert zu Boden.
English: He rises and walks towards the hearth. Sieglinde turns pale and, deeply moved, gazes at the floor.

[RS: Oper]
German: Kommandant verändert, erschüttert. Sieht nach seinen Soldaten. Auch dort knien einige. Er wendet sich rasch ab.
English: The commandant's manner has changed; he is shaken. He looks at his soldiers; some are kneeling there too. He quickly turns away.

【References】

Langenscheidt: erschüttert
Erschütterung
View examples▶Wagner Mahler R.Strauss
[GM], [RW: Oper], [RS: Oper]
Italian:
scossa, commozione

【General meanings】
① Vibration; shaking; disturbance; shock.
② Emotional shock; intense agitation; deep emotion.

【Examples in musical contexts】
[GM]
German: mit Erschütterung
English: With profound shock.

[RW: Oper]
German: Allgemeine Erschütterung und Trauer. Gunther bemüht sich um die Ohnmächtige.
English: Shock and grief spread through all present. Gunther tries to tend to the unconscious woman.

[RS: Oper]
German: Guntram, dessen Gesichtsausdruck und Haltung allmählich tiefste Erschütterung gewahren lassen, lässt sein Schwert fallen; in des Herzogs Augen blitzt es triumphirend auf.
English: Guntram’s expression and bearing gradually reveal his deep distress. He lets his sword fall; a triumphant gleam flashes in the Duke’s eyes.

【Usage notes】
In GM, the only example is in “Nun will die Sonn' so hell aufgeh'n,” the first song of Kindertotenlieder. “Mit Erschütterung” is translated here as “with profound shock.”

erst
View examples▶Wagner Mahler R.Strauss
[B: 2], [RW: Oper], [RS: Oper], [GM]
Italian:
solo, non prima di

【General meanings】
① (Time) only then; not until; finally.
② (Sequence) first; initially (the inflected forms erste, etc. mean “first” as an adjective).
③ (Degree or amount) only; merely.

【Examples in musical contexts】
[GM]
German: Anmerkung für den Dirigenten : In den ersten Takten des Thema's sind die Bassfiguren schnell in heftigem Ansturm ungefähr 𝅘𝅥 = 144, die Pausen jedoch im Hauptzeitmass 𝅘𝅥 = 84-92 auszuführen. Der Halt im 4. Takte ist kurz - gleichsam ein Ausholen zu neuer Kraft.
English: Note for the conductor: In the first bars of the theme, the figures in the low strings are to be played quickly, in a violent surge, at approximately quarter note = 144; the rests, however, are to be taken at the principal tempo, quarter note = 84–92. The fermata in the fourth bar is short, as if drawing back to gather fresh strength.

[RW: Oper]
German: Sie wirft das Seil zurück; die zweite Norn windet es auf, und wirft es der ersten wieder zu.
English: She (the Third Norn) throws the rope back; the Second Norn winds it up and throws it to the First again.

[RS: Oper]
German: wird jetzt erst gewahr, daß er nicht allein ist
English: Only now notices he is not alone.
ersterbend
View examples▶Wagner Mahler R.Strauss
[GM], [RW: Oper], [RS: Oper]
Italian:
morendo, perdendosi
Present participle of ersterben.

【General meanings】
① Gradually weakening and fading away.
② Dying or passing away (literary).

【Examples in musical contexts】
[GM]
German: ersterbend
English: As though dying away.

[RW: Oper]
German: beruhigend, ersterbend.
English: Soothingly, dying away.

[RS: Oper]
German: Erstes Blau aus den Schießscharten, seltsam vermischt mit dem dunkelroten Schein des ersterbenden Feuers.
English: The first blue light through the embrasures mingles strangely with the dark red glow of the dying fire.

【Usage notes】
“Fading away”; “gradually weakening”; “as though the sound were dying away”; “as though dying.”

In GM, I translate this as “as though dying,” although “fading away” would also work. GM also uses morendo in many passages, alongside ersterbend. Personally, I feel an emotional, introspective nuance in ersterbend, whereas morendo (which also derives from morire, “to die”) suggests “moving towards silence” or “fading away naturally.” I wonder what difference in nuance Mahler himself felt between them.

【References】
Duden: ersterben
Treccani: morendo
Erstes Zeitmaß, beschleunigt
[B: 3]
Resume the initial tempo, but at a quicker pace.

In [B: 3] (the 1889 version, Nowak edition), this marking occurs in the fourth movement at rehearsal W (bar 393). The preceding bar is marked accel.; the passage can thus be read as leading into the return of the initial-tempo section at an increased pace.

Bruckner: III. SYMPHONIE D-MOLL, 1889 version, p. 195 (PDF p. 197)
erzählen
View examples▶Wagner Mahler
[GM], [RW: Oper]
Italian:
raccontare, narrare

【General meanings】
① To tell; to relate; to narrate.
② To inform someone about something.

【Examples in musical contexts】
[GM]
German: erzählend und ohne Espressivo
English: Narratively and without espressivo

[RW: Oper]
German: Senta setzt sich erschöpft in den Lehnstuhl nieder; bei dem Beginn von Erik's Erzählung versinkt sie wie in magnetischen Schlaf, so dass es scheint als träume sie den von ihm erzählten Traum ebenfalls. - Erik steht an den Stuhl gelehnt zur Seite.
English: Exhausted, Senta sits down in the armchair. As Erik begins his story, she seems to sink into a magnetic sleep (i.e. a state resembling hypnosis, evoking the mesmerism popular in the nineteenth century), so that it appears she too is dreaming the dream he is recounting. Erik stands beside the chair, leaning against it.

【Usage notes】
The present participle erzählend can be rendered as “as though telling a story,” “in a narrative manner,” or “narratively.” In GM, the only examples occur in the sixth movement of DAS LIED VON DER ERDE.

Erzählung
View examples▶Wagner R.Strauss
[RW: Oper], [RS: Oper]
Italian:
racconto, narrazione

【General meanings】
① A story, tale, account, or short work of narrative fiction.
② The act of telling; narration.

【Examples in musical contexts】
[RW: Oper]
German: Sehr deutlich im Tone einer erregten Erzählung, durchaus verschieden von dem früheren Ausruf.
English: Very clearly, in the tone of an excited narrative, quite different from the earlier exclamation.

[RS: Oper]
German: Die Pagen haben jetzt ihre Stellung eingenommen vor den Königen und Königinnen. Sie imitieren die folgende Erzählung in einer Pantomime.
English: The pages have taken their places before the kings and queens. They enact the following account in pantomime.

【Usage notes】
“A story told within an opera, etc.”; “narration of events”; “an anecdote recounted within the drama.”

The word is used for a character’s account of events or experiences, or for the manner in which that account is delivered. For example, in Act I, Scene 3 of Tristan und Isolde WWV 90 in [RW: Oper], Isolde is directed to sing “in the tone of an agitated narration” (im Tone einer erregten Erzählung).

【References】

In performance directions, etwas modifies an adjective or adverb to temper its degree, and is translated as “somewhat,” “a little,” or similar expressions. In stage directions, it can also express a small difference in distance or position.

English: “At a somewhat moderate pace.”

German: etwas flüchtig = nachlässig
English: “With a swift, somewhat casual gesture.”

A direction concerning the execution of the eighth note in the motif.

[RW: Oper]
German: etwas frei
English: “Somewhat freely.”

German: von ihnen etwas entfernt
English: “A little apart from them.”

Describes a person's position on stage.

[RS: Oper]
German: etwas breit
English: “Somewhat broadly.”

German: Etwas mehr zur Mitte
English: “A little nearer the centre.”

Describes a person's position on stage.
etwas deutlicher u. allmälich ausdrucksvoller
[RS: Dom]
Somewhat more clearly, and gradually more expressively.

(Example: RS, Symphonia domestica Op.53, the ninth bar counting rehearsal 15 as bar 1, oboe d’amore.)

View examples▶Mahler
[GM]
Italian:
… volte, in … parti
A word element attached to a number (-fach).

【General meanings】
-Fold; multiplied or repeated the specified number of times.

【Examples in musical contexts】
[GM]
German: 4 fach geteilt
English: Divisi in four groups.

【Usage notes】
In a description of division with geteilt (older spelling getheilt), it indicates division into the specified number of parts or voices. The GM marking “2 fach getheilt” means that the strings are divided into two groups.
Distinguish this from the noun Fach: a compartment, a field of expertise, or a category of operatic role.

fahren
View examples▶Wagner R.Strauss
[RW: Oper], [RS: Oper]
Italian:
guidare, viaggiare

【General meanings】
① To travel in a vehicle; to drive.
② To move suddenly; to dart out; to make a sudden bodily movement.

【Examples in musical contexts】
[RW: Oper]
German: Man hört aus dem Gemerk unmutige Seufzer des Merkers und heftiges Anstreichen mit der Kreide. Auch Walther hat es gehört; nach kurzer Störung fährt er fort.
English: From inside the Gemerk (the marker’s booth), the marker’s disgruntled sighs and the sound of vigorous marking with chalk (on the blackboard) are heard. Walther hears them too; he is briefly unsettled but continues singing.

[RS: Oper]
German: Elektra fährt zusammen und starrt zuerst, wie aus einem Traum erwachend, auf Chrysothemis.
English: Elektra starts and at first stares at Chrysothemis as though waking from a dream.

【Usage notes】
For stage action, sense ② can be rendered as “to move swiftly.” Zurückfahren means “to recoil,” and fortfahren means “to continue.” Fahren lassen can also mean “to let go” or “to abandon.”

Fassung
[H: KM3]
Italian:
versione, redazione

【General meanings】
① A version, draft, or text of a written or artistic work; the wording of a law.
② A setting for a gem; a socket for a light bulb; a frame for spectacles.
③ Composure; calm; self-control.
④ Capacity; holding capacity.

【Usage notes】
For a composition, Fassung means a version or draft. It may refer to a revised version of an opera, for example, or a translated version of a vocal text. “A revised version” can be expressed as “revidierte Fassung,” but the context may also allow Fassung alone to refer to a particular revision or draft.

fest
View examples▶Wagner R.Strauss
[RS: Zara], [RS: Held], [RS: Alpen], [RW: Oper], [RS: Oper]
Italian:
fermo, saldo

【General meanings】
① Firm; solid; secure; fixed.
② Definite; settled; resolute, of the will, etc.
③ Constant; steady.

【Examples in musical contexts】
[RW: Oper]
German: Aus dem Hintergrunde schreitet, fest und feierlich, Brünnhilde dem Vordergrunde zu.
English: Brünnhilde advances from the back towards the front of the stage with a firm and solemn tread.

[RS: Oper]
German: betroffen hält sie einen Augenblick an, unterdessen ist ihr Guntram, der sich schnell gefasst hat, bereits nachgeeilt und hält sie fest
English: Startled, she pauses for a moment; meanwhile, Guntram, who has quickly regained his composure, has already hurried after her and holds her fast.

【Usage notes】
As a performance direction, fest can be rendered as “firmly.” In reference to tempo, possible renderings include “strictly,” “in tempo,” and “without altering the tempo.”
Festes is an inflected form of fest. In Wagner's Das Rheingold WWV 86A, the word is used in the sense of “solid.”

① Is found; is discovered; exists.

flüchtig
View examples▶Wagner Mahler R.Strauss
[GM], [RW: Oper], [RS: Oper]
Italian:
fugace, frettoloso, superficiale

【General meanings】
① Fleeting or short-lived; brief or done in passing.
② Hasty, superficial, or cursory.
③ Fleeing; on the run.
④ (Of a substance) Volatile.

【Examples in musical contexts】
[GM]
German: Sehr fließend, beinahe flüchtig
English: Very flowing, almost swift.

[RW: Oper]
German: Tannhäuser, der überrascht, schnell aufgefahren ist, faßt sich und verneigt sich stumm gegen den Landgrafen, nachdem er einen flüchtigen Blick auf ihn und die Sänger geworfen.
English: Tannhäuser, who has quickly sprung up in surprise, regains his composure and, after casting a fleeting glance at the Landgrave and the singers, bows silently to the Landgrave.

[RS: Oper]
German: Vor Aithra erscheint flüchtig ein und der andre Elf, gleichsam um ihre Befehle entgegenzunehmen, und verschwindet ebenso rasch.
English: One elf after another briefly appears before Aithra, as though to receive her commands, and vanishes just as swiftly.

【Usage notes】
“With a swift gesture”; “swiftly”; “as though flying away”; “fleetingly”; “(depending on the context) swiftly and somewhat casually.”

In Mahler’s SYMPHONIE V, the upbeat triplets at the opening of the first movement are marked flüchtig (quasi accel.), with an instruction to play them in the manner of military fanfares.

In the third movement, a footnote and musical example refer to the figure introduced by the first violins at rehearsal figure 6, “Etwas ruhiger.” They direct that the short note immediately after the eighth rest be played with a swift, somewhat casual gesture, whichever instrument takes up the figure.

For GM, I use “swiftly” as a broad common-denominator translation, even while wondering whether it fully reflects his intentions.

【References】

flüssig
View examples▶Mahler R.Strauss
[GM], [RS: Oper], [K: Cap]
Italian:
liquido, scorrevole

【General meanings】
① Liquid; fluid; molten.
② (Of actions or speech) smooth; fluent; unhesitating.
③ (Of funds, etc.) available; liquid.

【Examples in musical contexts】
[GM]
German: Nicht schleppen (etwas flüssiger als zu Anfang)
English: Do not drag (a little more fluently than at the beginning).

[RS: Oper]
German: flüssiger
English: More flowing.

【Usage notes】
In GM, the term occurs only in the fourth movement of SYMPHONIE V. It is translated here as “without hesitation.”

Reference score: Mahler, SYMPHONIE V (Peters edition): printed p. 178 / PDF p. 176

View examples▶Wagner Mahler R.Strauss
[GM], [RW: Oper], [RS: Oper]
Italian:
sussurrare

【General meanings】
① To whisper; to speak in a whisper.
② (Poetically or figuratively, of wind, leaves, etc.) To make a faint, whispering sound.

【Examples in musical contexts】
[GM]
German: flüsternd
English: As though whispering.

[RW: Oper]
German: Leise, flüsternd.
English: Softly, as though whispering.

[RS: Oper]
German: Aithra, die neben Menelas stand, gleitet lautlos zu Helena hinüber; was sie sagt, ist zum Schein zu Menelas gesprochen, in der Tat flüstert sie es Helena ein
English: Aithra, who has been standing beside Menelas, glides noiselessly over to Helena. Ostensibly she addresses Menelas, but in fact whispers her words to Helena.

【Usage notes】
In expressive performance directions, “as though whispering”; when describing the manner of speaking, “in a whisper.”

【References】

[GM], [RW: Oper], [RS: Oper]
Italian:

Third-person singular present of folgen.

【General meanings】
① (Of a person, thing, or event) follows; comes next.
② Follows or obeys (a rule or command, etc.); responds to.
③ Follows logically; ensues as a consequence.

【Examples in musical contexts】
[GM]
German: Folgt ohne jede Unterbrechung der 5. Satz
English: Proceed to the fifth movement without any interruption.

[RW: Oper]
German: Die Hölengruft erdämmert. Bläulicher Lichtschein: von ihm beleuchtet steigt mit dem Folgenden Erda sehr allmählich aus der Tiefe auf. Sie erscheint wie von Reif bedeckt; Haar und Gewand werfen einen glitzernden Schein von sich.
English: The cavern begins to glow dimly. A bluish light: illuminated by it, Erda rises very gradually from the depths during the following passage. She appears as if covered in frost; her hair and clothing give off a glittering sheen.

[RS: Oper]
German: Das folgende Gespräch wird so geführt, daß die andern auf der Szene anwesenden Personen es nicht hören; sie folgen mit ihrer ganzen Aufmerksamkeit dem vorgeführten Tanze
English: The following conversation is conducted so that the others onstage cannot hear it; they are giving their full attention to the dance.
folgt sofort der nächste Satz
[H: KM1-1]
Proceed immediately to the next movement.

(Hindemith, Kammermusik Nr. 1 für zwölf Solo-Instrumente Op.24/Nr.1, end of movement I.)

fort
View examples▶Wagner Mahler R.Strauss
[GM], [RW: Oper], [RS: Oper]
Italian:
via, avanti, continuamente

【General meanings】
① Away; gone; no longer present.
② Over; gone; no longer there.
③ Onwards; further; continuously; continuing.

【Examples in musical contexts】
[GM]
German: Marschierend, in einem fort
English: Marching, without interruption.

[RW: Oper]
German: Kurwenal eilt fort. - Tristan, in höchster Aufregung auf dem Lager sich mühend.
English: Kurwenal hurries away. Tristan, struggling on the couch in the utmost agitation.

[RS: Oper]
German: Die Kinder fahren desto eifriger im Tanze fort.
English: The children continue to dance all the more eagerly.

【Usage notes】
fort und fort means “continually” or “on and on”; in einem fort means “without stopping,” “all the time,” or “continuously.” In RW, Dämpfer fort is used to mean “remove the mutes.” No instance of this usage occurs in GM.
fort u. fort
[B: 4-2], [B: 5]
Italian:
continuamente, senza sosta
An expression formed with the adverb fort and und (abbreviated u.).

【General meanings】
Continuously; on and on; without interruption; persistently; ever onwards.
fort u. fort getragen
[B: 4-1]
Continuously, in a measured manner.

(Bruckner, IV. Symphonie Es-Dur "Romantische", 1874 version, movement IV, bar 51, oboes and clarinets.)

Frei im Vortrag
[RS: Alpen]
Italian:
libero nell’esecuzione, a piacere

【General meanings】
Freely and without stiffness in expression or delivery.

【Examples in musical contexts】
“Freely in musical expression”; “with flexible timing”; “with discretion in the manner of expression”; “with rubato.”

【Usage notes】
Vortrag here refers to the manner of performance or expression. The instruction can be understood as allowing freedom in the breathing and flow of the melody. In [RS: Alpen], it appears at rehearsal 77 in Auf dem Gipfel (“On the Summit”), over the first oboe’s melody, together with Etwas ruhiger (“somewhat calmer”). The melody is to be delivered freely, as if speaking, while maintaining its relationship with the string accompaniment.

früher
View examples▶Wagner Mahler R.Strauss
[GM], [RW: Oper], [RS: Oper]
Italian:
prima, precedente
Comparative of früh.

【General meanings】
① (In time) Earlier; sooner.
② (As an adverb) Previously; formerly; in the past.
③ (As an inflected adjective) Earlier; former.

【Examples in musical contexts】
[GM]
German: 𝅘𝅥. = wie früher 𝅘𝅥𝅮𝅘𝅥𝅮𝅘𝅥𝅮
English: Each dotted quarter note takes the same time as the earlier group of three triplet eighth notes.

[RW: Oper]
German: "Tod" nicht wie in früheren Ausgaben "Trank".
English: "Tod" (death), not "Trank" (potion) as in earlier editions.

[RS: Oper]
German: Die Statue verdunkelt sich wie Blei. Vor ihren Füßen hebt sich, wie früher, das goldene Wasser leuchtend empor.

English: The statue darkens like lead. At her feet the golden water rises brightly, as before.

【Usage notes】
wie früher means “as before”; when referring to tempo, “at the previous tempo.” noch früher means “at an even earlier point.”
führend
View examples▶Wagner R.Strauss
[RW: Oper], [RS: Zara], [RS: Oper]
Italian:
principale, guida
Present participle of führen.

【General meanings】
① Leading; guiding.
② Leading; principal; dominant in position or role.
③ Leading or extending (of a road, etc.).

【Examples in musical contexts】
[RW: Oper]
German: Durch aufsteigende gemauerte Gänge führend, hat die Szene sich vollständig verwandelt: Gurnemanz und Parsifal treten jetzt in den mächtigen Saal der Gralsburg ein.
English: After leading through ascending masonry passages, the scene has completely changed: Gurnemanz and Parsifal now enter the great hall of the Grail castle.

[RS: Oper]
German: Baron Ochs erscheint, den Arm in der Schlinge, Octavian an der Linken führend, hinter ihm der Leiblakai. Baron mustert den Raum. Octavian sieht herum, läuft an den Spiegel, richtet sein Haar.
English: Baron Ochs appears with his arm in a sling, leading Octavian with his left hand, with the Leiblakai behind him. The Baron surveys the room. Octavian looks around, runs to the mirror, and arranges his hair.

【Usage notes】
In music, “taking the lead,” “leading the melody,” or “as the principal part.” In [RS: Zara], it is contrasted with begleiten (“to accompany”). In RW, it has sense ① or ③.
für sich
View examples▶Wagner R.Strauss
[RW: Oper], [RS: Oper]
Italian:
per sé, da solo, separatamente

【General meanings】
① For oneself; by oneself.
② Alone; separately; apart from others.
③ In itself; considered on its own.
④ Privately; in confidence (in expressions such as etwas für sich behalten).

【Examples in musical contexts】
[RW: Oper]
German: Kleinmüthig, für sich.
English: Faint-heartedly, to himself.

[RS: Oper]
German: für sich, empört, halblaut
English: To himself, indignant, in a low voice.

【Usage notes】
für sich literally means “for oneself.” In contexts of speech or thought, the action is directed towards oneself rather than others, as in inward thought or speaking to oneself. Depending on context, possible translations include “inwardly,” “alone,” or “privately.”
By comparison, vor sich literally means “in front of oneself.” Expressions such as vor sich hin sprechen describe speaking to oneself, including muttering or speaking quietly. Possible translations include “as if talking to oneself” or “to oneself (aloud).”
Both expressions are often translated here as “as if talking to oneself.”

【References】
Duden: behalten; Stephan Bopp: vor sich hin

galant
View examples▶Wagner R.Strauss
[RS: Qui], [RW: Oper], [RS: Oper]
Italian:
galante, cortese

【General meanings】
① Courteous, polite, or gentlemanly; especially attentive towards women.
② Elegant, refined, or stylish.
③ Amorous; relating to love affairs.

【Examples in musical contexts】
[RW: Oper]
German: Luzio tritt auf, und nähert sich galant Isabella, ohne Dorella zu bemerken.
English: Luzio enters and approaches Isabella gallantly, without noticing Dorella.

[RS: Oper]
German: in höfisch galantem Ton
English: In a courtly, gallant tone.

【Usage notes】
“Elegantly”; “gracefully”; “with refinement”; “courteously”; “in a gentlemanly manner.”

At the opening of [RS: Qui], ritterlich und galant can be read as expressing a knightly spirit and an elegant manner. In operatic stage directions, galant also describes courteous treatment of another person or a graceful bow.

The historical social ideal of galant embraces wit and cultivated taste alongside courtesy and elegance.

【References】

ganz

[GM], [RW: Oper], [RS: Oper], [RS: Mac]
Italian:
intero, tutto, molto

【General meanings】
① (Adjectivally) Whole; entire; complete.
② (Adverbially) Completely; wholly; very.
③ (Modifying an adjective with a qualifying or moderate sense) Quite; fairly; reasonably, as in ganz gut.

【Examples in musical contexts】
[GM]
German: Quasi Tempo I, ganz wenig belebt
English: As if in Tempo I, very slightly animated.

[RW: Oper]
German: Während des Vorhergehenden hat sich nach und nach der ganze Jagdtroß des Landgrafen mit Falkenträgern u.s.w. auf der Bühne versammelt. Die Jäger stoßen in die Hörner.
English: During the preceding action, the Landgrave’s entire hunting party, accompanied by falconers carrying their birds and others, has gradually assembled on stage. The hunters sound their horns.

[RS: Oper]
German: sehr stark, ganz in der Nähe
English: Very loudly, very close.

【Usage notes】
im ganzen: “on the whole,” “generally,” “overall.”
ganze Takte means “whole bars.” In conducting directions such as ganze Takte schlagen, it is translated here as “in one”: beat each whole bar as a single beat.
ganz wenig: “very little.”

[GM], [RW: Oper], [RS: Oper]
Italian:
sordinato, smorzato
Past participle of dämpfen.

【General meanings】
① Softened, subdued, restrained.
② Dim (of light); muted (of colours).
③ Muted, damped, muffled (of sound); adverbially, “with subdued sound,” “with a muffled tone,” or “hushed.”

gehalten
View examples▶Wagner Mahler R.Strauss
[GM], [RW: Oper], [RS: Oper]
Italian:
tenuto, sostenuto, trattenuto
Past participle of halten.

【General meanings】
① Kept, held, maintained.
② Sustained, prolonged (of a sound or a duration).
③ Calm, reserved, restrained, measured.

【Examples in musical contexts】
[GM]
German: Gehaltener
English: With the tempo held back more.

[RW: Oper]
German: Sehr gemessen, vornehm, huldvoll gehalten.
English: Maintaining a very measured, refined and gracious manner.

[RS: Oper]
German: Zimmer des Sir Morosus, Weiter, unordentlich gehaltener Raum mit vielen Zeichen, die erkennen lassen, daß hier ein ehemaliger Seemann haust: Schiffsmodelle, Fahnen, Gewehre, Anker, Fischgerippe, Takelwerk. Besonders auffällig, daß alle Türen mit dichten Vorhängen oder Säcken geschützt sind.
English: Sir Morosus's room. A spacious, untidy room with many signs that a former sailor lives here: model ships, flags, guns, anchors, fish skeletons and rigging. Especially striking is the fact that all the doors are protected by thick curtains or sacks.

【Usage notes】
“With the notes sustained (sostenuto)”; “sustained (tenuto)”; “restrained”; “with a restrained tone.”

GM generally renders it as “with the tempo held back,” but the translation needs to vary according to context, using expressions such as “with the notes sustained” (≒ sostenuto) or “with a restrained flow.” It may refer to sustaining the tone fully and maintaining the flow of a phrase, or to keeping the tempo or expression calm and restraining the overall flow. These meanings may overlap; where the emphasis lies depends on the placement of the marking and the surrounding context. Sustaining tone and phrasing is close to the Italian sostenuto (“supported”) or tenuto (“held”), but is not a blanket instruction to lengthen every note beyond its written value.
The comparative form gehaltener also conveys the sense of “more” or “even more.”

By contrast, “anhalten” means “to hold back (something that is in motion), to bring it to a stop, or to apply the brakes”; in music, depending on the context, it is probably close to the Italian ritenuto (“immediately slower, held back”), which suggests holding the tempo back at that point.
See also the entry “anhalten.”

Gesangsperiode
[B: 4-2]
Italian:
periodo cantabile, periodo melodico
A compound noun formed from Gesang (“song”) + s (a linking element) + Periode (“period,” “span”).

【Examples in musical contexts】
“A cantabile period”; “a lyrical thematic section”; “the second theme group (especially in Bruckner's symphonies).”

This is a characteristic term used by Anton Bruckner for the “second theme group” in the sonata-form movements of his symphonies. It was not coined by Bruckner; rather, he is understood to have given substance, in keeping with his own sense of form, to a term derived from the compositional theory associated with Johann Christian Lobe. In German-language terminology, the first thematic area is called Hauptsatz or Hauptthema, and the second Seitensatz (secondary section) or Seitenthema (secondary theme). The closing area (often a third theme group in Bruckner) is called Schlusssatz (closing section) or Schlussthema (closing theme / third theme). In Bruckner, the second theme group is called Gesangsperiode (lyrical thematic section / singing period). Its character can be described as follows.

【Contrasts of character】

In Bruckner's sonata forms, the first theme (Hauptsatz) often has a “rhythmic, motivic, grand” character, contrasted with a second theme (Gesangsperiode) that is “melodic, lyrical (cantabile), and contrapuntal.” The following third theme (Schlusssatz) can display qualities such as “rhythmic energy, a powerful orchestral tutti, or a chorale-like character,” although these do not invariably occur together. This contrast suggests that the second theme is more than a merely subsidiary theme: it can be understood as a distinct, songful region (Periode).

【Structural independence】

Bruckner's “second theme” often forms an extended section (group), with several interwoven parts, rather than simply a single melody. It is therefore reasonable to describe it as a Periode (a section / a span) rather than only a Thema (theme).

The term is particularly characteristic of Bruckner and Bruckner scholarship when used for the second theme group in sonata form, but its background lies in nineteenth-century theories of form, including Lobe's.

【References】
Bruckner-Lexikon: Sonatenhauptsatzform

【Examples in musical contexts】
“With a thrusting bow stroke”; “detached”; “articulating the notes separately with the tongue (on a wind instrument)”.

【Usage notes】
It is translated here as “staccato”, except for kräftig gestoßen at bar 136 of SYMPHONIE VII, movement V. Since “with a strong staccato” seemed less suitable there, the translation chosen was “With strong articulation.”

The degree of separation and emphasis depends on the instrument and the surrounding directions. The passage above also carries the marking p marcato. Strong articulation does not necessarily mean a loud dynamic.

gestrichen
View examples▶Mahler R.Strauss
[GM], [RS: Oper], [B]
Italian:
arcato — bowed (of a string instrument)
barrato — crossed out; deleted
Past participle of the verb streichen (to stroke, rub, or cross out).

【General meanings】
① Stroked or rubbed.
② Applied (of paint, etc.).
③ Crossed out or deleted (of letters, text, etc.).
④ Bowed (of a string instrument).

【Examples in musical contexts】
“Sustained (with a long bow stroke)”; “drawn out (with a long bow stroke)”; “using a full bow (in Bruckner)”; “played with the bow”; “deleted”.

The word can also refer to octave notation. The prime sign (′) placed to the upper right of a note name is called a Strich (stroke); the number of these strokes indicates which octave the note belongs to. For example, dreimal gestrichenes C means “three-line C”.

【Use of gestrichen in Bruckner】
The word is used to call for ample bowing and a clear profile for individual notes. Besides a return to ordinary bowing, it may concern fullness of tone or a separate bow stroke for each note. Changing bow direction for each note does not necessarily mean leaving a silence between notes.

【Use of gezogen in Bruckner】
The word suggests using ample bow and sustaining a full tone. The German verb ziehen (to draw or pull) has connotations of drawing a line and extending something at length. Oeser discusses lang gezogen, gezogen, gestrichen, and kurz gestrichen as differentiated directions within the practice of bowing each note separately. In his account, fullness of tone and a clear melodic profile go together.

When considering Bruckner’s sound, the metaphor “organ-like” may offer a useful image for sustaining a full tone. The actual bow speed and pressure are adjusted according to the dynamics, register, phrasing, and other circumstances.

In SYMPHONIE V, movement I, the cellos and double basses are marked “gestrichen, mehr gezogen” at bar 174 and “gestrichen, gezogen” at bar 176, with both words combined in the same direction.

【Use of gestrichen in GM】
After special techniques such as pizz. or col legno, gestrichen (or wieder gestrichen) can indicate a return to ordinary bowing. There are also examples such as breit gestrichen, kurz gestrichen, and lang gestrichen that describe the breadth or length of the bow stroke. For example, breit gestrichen is translated here as “With broad bow strokes.” and kurz gestrichen as “With short bow strokes.”

【Use of gezogen in GM】
The collected examples include breit gezogen, lang gezogen, and lang gezogen (viel Bogen). The adopted translations are “Play with long (ample) bow strokes.” for lang gezogen and “Play with long (ample) bow strokes (using plenty of bow).” for lang gezogen (viel Bogen).

It is best not to read Bruckner’s directions concerning bowing or sonority simply as a return to arco. Thinking of GM’s return instructions as “How to play” and Bruckner’s directions concerning fullness of tone as “How it sounds” may help bring out the differences between these contexts. Playing technique and sound are, however, connected in both composers.

【References】

Italian:
sostenuto, grave
Past participle of tragen.

【General meanings】
① Carried (of luggage, etc.); worn (of clothes, etc.).
② Grave, dignified, or solemn (of manner, gait, etc.).

【Examples in musical contexts】
[GM]
German: Nicht eilen. Immer dasselbe getragene Zeitmass.
English: Do not hurry. Always keep the same unhurried tempo.

[RW: Oper]
German: Erster Zug von links. 15 Ritter. Knappen. Gralsträger. Amfortas getragen. zweiter Zug von rechts. 15 Ritter. Leiche Titurels von 4 Dienern getragen. Die Leiche wird mit dem Gesicht gegen den Altar gestellt.
English: First procession from the left. 15 Ritter. Knappen. Gralsträger. Amfortas carried (on a stretcher). Second procession from the right. 15 Ritter. Titurel’s body carried by four attendants. The body is placed with its face towards the altar.

[RS: Oper]
German: sehr getragen, aber nicht stark
English: Very sustained, but not loud.

【Usage notes】
“sustaining the tone fully”, “solemnly”, “gravely”, “maintaining a slow tempo”.

As an adjectival use of the past participle of tragen (to carry or support), the word conveys calmness and weight of tone, rather than merely the physical speed indicated by langsam (slow). It may suggest an inward gravity supported by rich, deep tone, but does not itself specify breath or bow pressure. It is close to sostenuto or grave. In GM, many occurrences are translated as “unhurriedly”, despite the possible loss of some of this nuance.

【References】

【General meanings】
① To win a contest or battle; to gain victory.
② To gain, obtain, or acquire something (profit, an object, a position, etc.).

[GM]
